Q: Environment-Specific Configuration Values During a Jenkins + Maven Build A:

Thank you Meier,

in your way each environment requires a cloned configuration file, and these files can contain hundreds of entries. As a result, any fix or change must be manually replicated across all configuration files—we currently maintain configurations for eight different servers. This approach is error-prone and difficult to maintain.

The design I am proposing simplifies this by introducing a single properties file per environment. Each file would contain only environment-specific configurations, significantly reducing duplication and making updates more efficient, consistent, and easier to manage.

Q: gfortran compiler flag for strict Fortran 77 compliance A:

I would have also tried it with a couple of gfortran compiler flags.

If you are flexible with additional libraries there is another Fortran 77 compiler besides f77. It is called cf77 from Concurrent. It is a compiler including some real time libraries. Here you can find the Documentation

As I remember there is still a license fee. But this compiler supports pure f77 and still has the old libraries included.

Another option could be using the g77 compiler and eventually downgrading your available libraries. Here is a Manual for the g77 compiler.

Q: How to hide an API key in SvelteKit so it's not visible in the browser? A:

Server-only modules:

Like a good friend, SvelteKit keeps your secrets. When writing your backend and frontend in the same repository, it can be easy to accidentally import sensitive data into your front-end code (environment variables containing API keys, for example). SvelteKit provides a way to prevent this entirely: server-only modules.

  1. Use your (hardcoded) API key in an internal +server API endpoint.
  2. Call your internal API endpoint from +page.svelte
  3. Optional: instead of hardcoding, put your API key in a private env variable. Now your API key will not be in your git commit history and Svelte will warn you if you accidentally use it from a browser-visible file.

Examples of how I've used this method in action in my weather-sense project:

  • API key used in src/routes/api/geo/reverse/+server.ts
  • internal API called from src/lib/weather/shell.ts
  • There is no way to get the value of OPEN_WEATHER_APPID from the browser (you can try here: https://weather-sense.leftium.com)
